title: Terraform provider pinning, upgrade playbook, and post-upgrade health checks for Private VPC
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a conservative, auditable strategy for pinning Terraform module and provider versions used by Private (VPC) deployments, produce an automated upgrade playbook (including CI jobs), and add post-upgrade health checks and smoke tests. Goal: eliminate surprise breakages during routine provider/module upgrades and provide repeatable rollback steps for high-risk infra changes.
acceptance_criteria: A documented version pinning policy that maps modules to provider version constraints and upgrade windows
A templated upgrade playbook that operators can run end-to-end with >95% automation
CI pipeline changes that run a non-destructive plan, drift detection, and a dry-run smoke test in a staged environment
Automated post-upgrade health checks (control plane, node agents, networking, KMS access) with alerts and dashboard links
Rollback steps validated in a lab run (recorded) and a tested Terraform state backup/restore procedure
technical_plan: Inventory: scan all private-vpc Terraform repos for module and provider blocks; produce a CSV mapping module_name, module_version, provider, provider_version_constraint
Pinning policy: recommend exact pinning for providers that change breaking behavior (e.g., aws, azuread), semver-minor pinning for safe providers, and documented exceptions
Compatibility matrix: for each module, list tested provider versions and required migration steps (inline in README and a single source of truth CSV)

Playbook: create a CI-driven playbook that performs: terraform init with -get=true, terraform plan (no changes) in staging, apply in canary workspace, post-apply checks, promote to remaining workspaces
State safety: snapshots to remote S3/GCS with versioning and server-side encryption before any upgrade; mandatory state-lock via DynamoDB/CloudSQL
Policy gates: add terraform-validate + custom checks (policy as code or OPA) to block known unsafe upgrades
Automation: provide a Makefile/CLI wrapper (scripts/upgrade-provider.sh) to automate plan/apply/validate steps and emit a detailed report
upgrade_steps: Step 0 - Pre-flight: run inventory job and create state snapshot; notify stakeholders
Step 1 - Staging: bump provider/module pins in staging branch, terraform init -upgrade, run terraform plan, review plan output and resource replacement risk
Step 2 - Canary: apply changes to a single canary workspace/region (automated); run full health check suite
Step 3 - Monitor: 30m to 2h active monitoring window with automated rollback triggers on SLO degradation
Step 4 - Promote: if canary healthy, roll sequentially to remaining workspaces with automated plan/apply and health checks
Step 5 - Post-mortem: collect run artifacts, plan logs, and alerts; update compatibility matrix
health_checks: Control plane API latency and error rate (Redwood private control plane): expected <200ms p95, error rate <0.5%
Agent heartbeat: all edge/node agents report last_seen <60s
KV cache sanity: verify example inference request returns correct cached prefix headers
Networking: VPC peerings and route tables validated via test harness (ping/curl to internal endpoints)
KMS: perform a key encrypt/decrypt call using customer-managed key to verify permissions
S3/GCS access: test state backend read/write with identical IAM role used in production
Terraform plan idempotency: re-run plan after apply and ensure no further changes
Application smoke: run basic generation request against canary model endpoint and verify token-level response and latency
rollback_plan: If critical errors are detected during canary or early rollout, trigger automated revert: terraform apply using pre-upgrade state snapshot and pinned provider versions
If automated revert fails, escalate to on-call infra + on-call runtime engineers; open incident with 'tf-provider-upgrade' tag
Recreate state from snapshot in isolated workspace and validate resource consistency before re-promote
Document root cause and plan a safe reattempt schedule with smaller canaries or patching modules
ci_cd_changes: Add inventory scan job (weekly) that emits module/provider CSV to infra-artifacts bucket
New pipeline: terraform-upgrade-playbook that executes in a staging environment, requires manual approval to proceed to canary
Add post-apply health-check workflow that runs smoke tests and writes results to Ops dashboard (PagerDuty hooks)
Add auto-created PR template that includes compatibility CSV diff and risk classification
notes: Avoid broad -upgrade in daily CI; only use for controlled upgrade jobs
We should treat provider upgrades as code changes: require standard PR review + infra SME approval
Some older modules use provider aliases which complicate pinning; plan to refactor aliases in a follow-up
Consider adding a lightweight canary environment per region to reduce blast radius
